- Linux `mlockall(3)` requests current and future mappings; Windows requests working-set bounds `(-1,-1)`. Both are best-effort, not a verified no-swap guarantee. Independently, systemd scope asks `MemorySwapMax=0` and, at systemd >=253, `MemoryZSwapMax=0`.
- Systemd scope re-exec uses `systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --same-dir --collect --slice=app-mlps-training.slice --description=tabular:<label>`, with CPU/IO weight and startup weight 10000, TasksMax infinity, CPU/IO/memory/task accounting enabled, and current affinity as `AllowedCPUs` when available. It skips non-POSIX, explicit skip/scoped env, `python -c`/`-` execution, or absent `systemd-run`; exec failure falls back in the current process.

## 18. Central-runner helper and record contracts

- `_truthy` strips and lowercases; true tokens are `1,true,yes,on,y`, false tokens are `0,false,no,off,n` and empty string; missing or unrecognized values use the caller-provided default. `_parent_cpu_masked` returns true for backend `cpu`, a present CUDA visibility string that strips to empty or `-1`, or any truthy `CPU_ONLY`, `TRAINING_CONTROL_CPU_ONLY`, or `OPF_ADP_DISABLE_GPU_ACCELERATORS`.
- `_env_int`/`_env_float` return the given default only when the variable is absent or cannot be parsed; they are currently unused in this runner. `_safe_int`/`_safe_float` similarly catch conversion exceptions and use a provided fallback.
- `_ensure_dir` uses recursive `mkdir(exist_ok=True)`. `_atomic_write_text` ensures the parent, writes `<suffix>.tmp`, then replaces the target; it does not explicitly fsync. JSON is sorted, indented by two spaces, then uses that text replacement. Event CSV opens append mode, writes a header only when the path did not exist before opening, ignores extra row keys, flushes and attempts `fsync`; header/write failures are not caught by the helper. Timestamp strings use local time formatted `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S` (not UTC).
- `_json_signature` hashes UTF-8 canonical JSON with sorted keys, compact separators, and ASCII escaping using SHA-256. `_load_json` catches all read/parse errors and returns the supplied default. `_write_csv_row` is append-only and writes a new header only for a new file.
- `load_batch_backoff_state` reads `batch_backoff_state.json`; unreadable/non-dict content becomes `{}`. It fills missing fields with defaults: scale `1.0`, pending false, reason/time null; both launch lanes enabled; both gates open and lock IDs null; GPU/host buffers `100/500 MiB`; holds, pressure-used baselines, last-child footprints/remaining-memory and external memory/PID tracking all zero/empty/null. Existing values, including stale transient values, are retained by this loader. `normalize_dual_gate_state` only adds missing dual-gate, lock, buffer, hold, pressure-baseline, child-footprint and external-tracking fields; it does not normalize `batch_scale` or backoff reason/time. In `main()`, the subsequent invocation reset overwrites transient fields before writing the initial state, so those prior values are not used to continue admission/backoff across invocations.
- `_parse_csv_ints`, `_parse_range_tuple`, and `_format_kv` have no in-file call sites. The first converts nonempty comma-separated tokens to integers; the second requires exactly two nonempty integers and raises `ValueError` otherwise; the third emits booleans as lowercase text, primitive values via `str`, and other values as sorted JSON.
- `_proc_group_kwargs` starts a new POSIX session; on Windows it uses `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` only if the platform exposes a nonzero flag. Central termination itself uses psutil process-tree traversal rather than `killpg`: if the root handle already exited it returns; if the root PID cannot be opened it best-effort calls `Popen.terminate()` and returns without waiting. Otherwise it snapshots descendants recursively, terminates descendants in reverse enumeration order, terminates the root, waits at least 0.1s and up to the configured timeout, then kills survivors, waits again, kills any still alive a second time, and best-effort waits for the root. Default timeout is 10 seconds. `_close_runtime_log_handle` best-effort flushes/closes and always clears the runtime handle.
- `MemorySample` carries total/available/used-percent plus swap total/used/used-percent. `GpuMemorySample` carries total/used/free MiB and used percent. `JobSpec` is frozen and carries deterministic job identity, command, dimensions, and a `device_capable` field that is only serialized. `JobRuntime` carries process/log handles, device, attempts/retries, pause state and counters, legacy OOM lane flag, exit/timestamps and last-progress time. Its derived status priority is: ended with exit 0 => completed; live process => running; paused flag => paused; no exit code => queued; otherwise failed. `RecoveredProcessHandle.poll()` returns `None` while the PID passes live/non-zombie checks and synthetic `1` after disappearance; the latter is intercepted as unknown status before ordinary exit classification.
- `_write_compat_state_views` writes candidate state first, then recomputes method/task/replay views by scanning sorted job directories. Unknown state statuses count as queued; `launching` counts as running. Completed requires status completed and safe integer exit code 0. Latest completed is sorted by numeric-like ended timestamp then job ID. `best_candidate_dir` is simply the first successful result in the sorted discovered-state order, not a score-based best. The event aggregator may scan state files that are not in this run's manifest.

## 19. Static contract tests: scope and limits

The copied suite has operational contract tests for latest-launch-only failure classification, CUDA/cuDNN/cuBLAS OOM markers, pressure reopen domains, ordinary lane selection after OOM, CPU-parent backend masking, retry limit zero, persisted relaunch failure, source-presence of child-pressure gates, manifest equivalence under interpreter symlink aliases, progress fallback/scoping, termination-based central pause followed by a new-PID relaunch, bundle traversal rejection/chunking/shard checksum, owned-process matching (including rejection of a `py_compile` command that merely names the runner script), and standalone POSIX stop/continue. The manifest tests also inspect default grid generation, deterministic repeat-specific seeds, epoch zero/unlimited handling, cap propagation, and argument validation.

These are test definitions inspected statically, not test results. `test_massive_scheduler_operational_contract.py` pins the source Git blob as `d1bf6afe6edda9bbcaac4fe8dde79346b4db6034`, while the copied scheduler hashes to a different blob recorded in Section 13; that source-identity test is expected to fail against this snapshot. The manifest/progress tests also include model, architecture, and task-data assertions excluded from this orchestration ledger. Two child checkpoint handoff contracts are relevant here: training engines must pass stage checkpoint mirror paths when calling telemetry checkpoint writers, and telemetry mirror helpers write identical checkpoint bytes to telemetry and stage paths. These are source/test contracts rather than runtime results. No tests were run in this audit.

## 20. Child stage checkpoint and exact-resume contracts

This section covers the shared checkpoint utilities because the central runner's pressure pause kills a child and relies on the next child launch to resume its prior work. It omits model-layer semantics and OPF data/metric payloads.

### `resume_state.py` (`DNN/VANILLA/Dyn_DNN4OPF/utils/resume_state.py`, 271 lines)

- Checkpoint schema is integer `2`. `load_exact_checkpoint(path,map_location)` loads with `weights_only=False`, wraps any load error or non-dict payload as `RuntimeError` prefixed `exact-resume failure`.
- `atomic_checkpoint_save` creates the destination directory, makes a uniquely named temporary in that same directory, `torch.save`s, fsyncs the temp file, atomically `os.replace`s the target, fsyncs the directory using `O_DIRECTORY`, then removes any leftover temp in `finally`. This is stronger durability than telemetry JSON/Torch helpers, which replace but do not fsync.
- `save_initial_training_checkpoint` is a no-op for absent path or an existing path unless `overwrite=True`. Otherwise it snapshots architecture/state and writes schema, `epoch=0`, `global_batch=0`, model/optimizer/scheduler state, `best_val=inf`, best and best-batch snapshots equal to the initial snapshot, `best_batch_loss=inf`, integer patience, and captured training state. Scheduler state is `None` when no `state_dict` method exists.
- Captured RNG includes Python `random`, Torch CPU, all CUDA RNG states only when CUDA is available and initialized (else empty list), and NumPy state if NumPy imports (else `None`). Captured loader/backend state includes train sampler `state_dict` if available; train/validation generator states; cuDNN deterministic/benchmark and Torch deterministic-algorithm flags; loader contract; Torch and CUDA version strings.
- Torch/CUDA runtime versions are recorded for provenance but `restore_training_state` does not compare them to the current runtime. CUDA RNG is not required by the validation path; it is restored only when CUDA is available and saved CUDA states are nonempty. Backend state is optional at restore; when present, missing deterministic keys default to false.
- Loader contract is absent for no loader or objects without `.dataset`; otherwise it records fully qualified dataset and sampler types, dataset length, batch size, and `drop_last` boolean.
- `restore_training_state` rejects schema below 2. Compatibility inference of absent `global_batch` is narrowly allowed only when the saved sampler is explicitly exhausted, its order is a complete permutation of the current dataset indices, and current sampler can load state; then it mutates payload cursor to zero. It requires model, optimizer, epoch, and cursor, plus scheduler except for `training_kind == "adp_external_adapter_no_scheduler"`.
- External-adapter checkpoints additionally require `best_val`, `best_state`, `es_counter`, `history`, `train_epoch_log_accum`, `train_epoch_n`. A payload with `patience` requires ADP best-validation/best-batch snapshots and losses. Otherwise a payload with `early_stop_counter` requires native best/epoch-loss/history fields. This branching classifies checkpoint payload families; it does not relax RNG/loader requirements.
- Python and Torch CPU RNG state are mandatory; NumPy state is mandatory when NumPy is installed. If loader generators exist, their saved states must be Torch tensors. A positive batch cursor requires a saved shuffled order and a current sampler exposing `load_state_dict`. A current DataLoader contract requires a saved contract; any saved/current mismatch is fatal.
- Restore order is sampler state (`replay_current_epoch` iff cursor > 0), train/validation loader generator states, backend deterministic flags (using `warn_only=True`), then RNG. Mid-epoch loaders exposing `defer_rng_restore` defer global RNG until iterator creation so replacement-iterator seed consumption does not alter continuation. Exceptions are wrapped as exact-resume `RuntimeError`; a false RNG restore is a `ValueError`.

### `checkpoint_utils.py` (`DNN/VANILLA/Dyn_DNN4OPF/models/checkpoint_utils.py`, 373 lines)

- `load_checkpoint_snapshot` returns `None` for absent/unreadable/non-mapping or snapshot-less files; it loads to the supplied device with `weights_only=False`, retrying without that keyword only on `TypeError`, and returns `best_snap` only when it is a mapping.
- `restore_stage_architecture` requires a nonempty `current_hidden_widths` list/tuple. It first uses an existing `stage_checkpoint`; if absent, it may resolve `stage_architecture_checkpoint` relative to `Path(stage_checkpoint).resolve().parents[2]`, rejecting absolute paths and `..`. The checkpoint must contain matching snapshot `hidden_widths`; it calls `restore_arch_and_state`, then restores controller RNG. If no usable checkpoint restore path exists, it calls `_rebuild_hidden_layers` or `_rebuild`, restores `_width_growth_cursor`, and restores controller RNG. Failures are fatal exact-resume errors.
- Controller RNG restore is skipped when the sidecar says active stage and the stage checkpoint exists: the active training checkpoint owns RNG. Otherwise it accepts a relative in-results `rng_checkpoint_path` or a local `rng_checkpoint` filename that resolves uniquely under results; loads CPU and delegates to `restore_rng_state`. Absolute/traversal paths, missing/ambiguous files, or invalid RNG fail closed.
- Architecture matching compares `hidden_widths`, falling back to uniform `(width,)*depth`; absent/non-mapping snapshots fail closed. `restore_stage_checkpoint` requires a readable best checkpoint and architecture snapshot and restores it through `model.restore_arch_and_state`.
- `discover_exact_active_depth_stage` scans `stages/NNN_*` latest-first. A candidate `checkpoint_last.pt` must have schema >=2 and fields for model/optimizer/scheduler, epoch/cursor, RNG/sampler/loader/backend, best snapshots/losses/patience. At cursor zero it requires an exhausted sampler; positive cursor requires saved order. It requires complete Python/Torch/NumPy RNG, dictionary loader/backend contracts, a valid current architecture vector, exactly one preceding stage directory with `stage_state.json`, a readable best checkpoint snapshot, `best_val`/`best_depth`, and at least one failure counter. A relative `best_checkpoint` in the prior-stage summary is interpreted against process `cwd`, not the result root, and no root-containment check is applied to that path. For round-robin aliases, missing width cursor is reconstructed as zero only while still inside the depth-growth chain. Returns an active-stage recovery record with best/current architecture, counters, stage checkpoint, and `legacy_stage_recovery=True`; malformed candidates are skipped, and no candidate returns `None`.
- `load_partial_state_dict` copies same-shaped tensors exactly; for same-rank shape mismatches it copies the origin-aligned overlap hyperrectangle into the freshly initialized target tensor. Missing keys, non-tensors, rank mismatch, or zero-size overlap are skipped. Loads the merged dict with `strict=False`; optional logger receives copied/skipped counts and logger errors are ignored.
- `restore_stage_last_checkpoint` is a permissive completed-stage recovery: missing/unreadable model state returns false, otherwise partial-loads into the current model and logs exceptions. `restore_stage_last_checkpoint_exact` requires schema >=2, exact architecture match, mapping model state, then strict-loads; ordinary unusable state returns false, thrown exceptions become exact-resume failure.

## 21. Child telemetry and stage sidecar integration

`DNN/VANILLA/Dyn_DNN4OPF/utils/run_telemetry.py` is 1,337 lines. Task-specific metric computation and output schema are excluded; the orchestration contract is its durable progress, stage-state, checkpoint path, and resume logic.

- `TrainingTelemetry.__post_init__` uses `<results>/telemetry/<safe-model>/<safe-case>/task_<id:04d>/` and creates `telemetry.csv`, `progress_state.json`, `stage_state.json`, `checkpoint_last.pt`, `checkpoint_best.pt`, and `checkpoint_best_batch.pt`. Slugging lowercases and maps non-alphanumerics to `_`, collapses repeats, and falls back to `unknown`.
- JSON conversion serializes scalar tensors to Python scalars, non-scalar tensors to lists, paths to strings, and recursively converts dict/list/tuple values. JSON/text writes use a sibling `<suffix>.tmp` then replace; Torch checkpoint helper does the same. These helpers do not fsync. CSV append creates a header only when the file did not exist before open, ignores extra fields, JSON-encodes dict/list cells, renders `None` as empty, and appends one row.
- Startup progress counters prefer a readable `progress_state.json` (`history_rows`, `final_epoch`); malformed/missing state falls back to CSV `record_type` or `kind` values exactly `batch` and `epoch`. CSV read failure resets both counters to zero.
- `record_batch` appends a batch row, increments `batches_done`, then rewrites progress state. `record_epoch` appends an epoch row, increments `epochs_done` only when payload kind defaults to or equals `epoch`, then rewrites progress state. `update_state` appends a state row and rewrites progress state without incrementing counts. Progress JSON schema is `1` and stores identity, counters, timestamp plus current kind/stage/split/epoch/batch/cursor/patience/architecture/best-loss/checkpoint/active-stage/artifact fields.
- `save_stage_state` captures Python/NumPy/Torch RNG into a uniquely named `stage_state.rng.<time_ns>.<uuid>.pt`, records model/case/phase/task, schema `2`, RNG basename and path relative to results, atomically writes stage JSON, appends a `stage_state` CSV row, and rewrites progress JSON. Old RNG companion files are not pruned here.
- `refresh_active_stage_architecture` only acts when a readable non-completed active sidecar points to the exact supplied checkpoint. It requires callable `model.hidden_widths()`, nonempty result, then records integer widths/cursor and a reconciliation marker through `save_stage_state`.
- `load_stage_state` prefers `stage_state.json`; malformed JSON/non-object errors are fatal. A valid active stage checkpoint with exact RNG state becomes RNG authority and defers sidecar RNG. Active sidecar architecture disagreement with a loadable checkpoint is fatal unless the narrow in-stage depth-growth reconciliation predicate accepts the checkpoint. If the expected canonical active checkpoint is not written yet, it returns the sidecar and defers RNG until architecture rebuild. Legacy active checkpoints that are not complete exact checkpoints return `None` so controller discovery can inspect them. A sidecar with current widths and stage checkpoint defers RNG until after architecture rebuild. Other sidecars restore their RNG companion immediately; absent/invalid RNG is fatal unless exact active checkpoint state supersedes it.
- When JSON sidecar is absent, the code attempts recovery from the last matching `stage_state` CSV row filtered by model/case/phase/task ID. CSV `completed` strings are explicitly parsed as true only for `1,true,yes,y,on`; other CSV values remain strings. Then the same active-checkpoint/RNG deferral rules apply. However, the current CSV column schema/base-row writer does not persist `active_stage`, `current_hidden_widths`, `current_width_growth_cursor`, `stage_checkpoint`, or RNG companion names. Consequently a current-writer CSV row cannot prove the active-stage exact-checkpoint predicate and normally reaches `_restore_stage_rng` without `rng_checkpoint`, which raises exact-resume failure. This is a partial/legacy lookup path, not a working substitute for the JSON stage sidecar under the current writer.
- Exact active-checkpoint validation requires canonical path `<results>/stages/NNN_<stage>/checkpoint_last.pt` within results, schema >=2, model/optimizer/scheduler, epoch/cursor, RNG/sampler, best snapshots/losses/patience, loader/backend dicts, and complete Python/Torch/NumPy RNG. Positive cursor requires sampler order. Snapshot and sidecar width vectors must match, or the narrow depth-stage recovery must prove same stage index, start/target bounds, nondecreasing per-layer widths, matching architecture length, and matching tensor key/shape sets between best snapshot and model state. Accepted reconciliation updates sidecar widths/cursor and marks it.
- `save_last_checkpoint`, `save_best_checkpoint`, and `save_best_batch_checkpoint` write the telemetry-local checkpoint and optionally mirror the same payload to a caller path; these are replace-based writes without the `fsync` durability protocol used by `resume_state.atomic_checkpoint_save`.
- The telemetry object also implements a text-file compatibility surface over stage JSON: `exists()` means `load_stage_state()` returned a value; `read_text()` returns sorted/indented JSON or empty text; `write_text()` parses JSON, or wraps invalid text as `{kind: stage_state, raw_text: ...}`, then persists dicts via `save_stage_state` and returns input length. Restoring through these methods can capture RNG again because `load_stage_state()` applies its normal defer/restore rules.

## 22. Windows outer supervisor and small launcher wrappers

- `run_massive_opf_suite.ps1` sets `$ErrorActionPreference="Stop"`, changes to snapshot root, dot-sources `_OrphanWatchdog.ps1` and PowerShell defaults, chooses local venv Python or literal `python`, and defaults results/run/source roots to `Results/massive_opf_suite`, `<results>/run_root`, and `<results>/source_run_root`. It casts stop/resume environment values to doubles for its banner, but scheduler values are also sourced through the defaults and passed by launcher environment/CLI.
- Windows truth parsing recognizes only `1,true,yes,on,y` after trim/lowercase; unknown/empty is false. Thermal guard defaults enabled unless explicitly set false. Surface/tasks default `all`; optional param band, legacy grid, small STL, vanilla, missing-present-task repeats (1), and prediction repeats (1) are forwarded. Vanilla defaults true when env is absent/blank; otherwise parsed truth controls it.
- Before launch it removes stale `thermal_guard.stop`, snapshots current power-scheme GUID if `powercfg` exists, and may start `strong_awake_guard.ps1` and `thermal_guard_embedded.ps1` minimized. It launches Python unbuffered with `utils\opf_suite_launcher.py --mode massive --results-dir ... --run-root ... --source-run-root ... --surface ... --tasks ...`, adds optional flags and caller args, then starts a master watchdog against the launcher PID and waits. Nonzero launcher exit throws.
- `finally` writes stop file, force-stops thermal and awake helpers, stops/removes watchdog and event subscription, force-stops launcher if still live, restores the captured power scheme best-effort, and removes stop file. A thermal guard may create/select High Performance while running; outer wrapper restores the prior active scheme.
- `thermal_guard_embedded.ps1` defaults hot/cool labels 90/85 C, `HotCpuMax=100`, `NormalCpuMax=100`, poll 5 sec; hot/cool/HotCpuMax are unused for throttling. It selects the first listed High Performance scheme, or duplicates base scheme `8c5e7fda-e8bf-4a96-9a85-a6e23a8c635c`, then activates it. Every poll reapplies AC display timeout 5 minutes; standby/hibernate/disk timeout 0; power subgroup `238c9fa8-0aad-41ed-83f4-97be242c8f20` settings `29f6c1db-86da-48c5-9fdb-f2b67b1f44da=0`, `9d7815a6-7ee4-497e-8888-515a05f02364=0`, `94ac6d29-73ce-41a6-809f-6363ba21b47e=0`, `7bc4a2f9-d8fc-4469-b07b-33eb785aaca0=0`, `25dfa149-5dd1-4736-b5ab-e8a37b5b8187=1`; power-button subgroup `4f971e89-eebd-4455-a8de-9e59040e7347`, setting `5ca83367-6e45-459f-a27b-476b1d01c9360=0`; processor subgroup `54533251-82be-4824-96c1-47b60b740d00`, minimum `893dee8e-2bef-41e0-89c6-b55d0929964c=5`, maximum `bc5038f7-23e0-4960-96da-33abaf5935ec=NormalCpuMax`, cooling `94d3a615-a899-4ac5-ae2b-e4d8f634367f=0`. It sets `SetThreadExecutionState(CONTINUOUS|SYSTEM_REQUIRED|AWAYMODE_REQUIRED)`, samples maximum CPU temperature from LibreHardwareMonitor, then OpenHardwareMonitor, then ACPI thermal zones; logs only and sleeps `PollSeconds`. Stop file ends loop; `finally` resets execution state to continuous. Errors are globally silenced. It does not implement thermal throttling. The outer wrapper only restores the previously active scheme; it does not roll back values changed on the High Performance scheme or delete a newly duplicated scheme. In its `finally`, it writes the stop file and immediately force-stops the thermal process without waiting for the helper to observe the file.
- Per-case shell wrappers only set case name/tag and default `INCLUDE_VANILLA=1`, then exec `run_case_suite.sh`; that common wrapper errors if case name is empty and execs launcher mode `case`. Search wrapper defaults tasks `vanilla,width_only,width_to_depth`, surface `all`; width/depth parallel wrapper defaults `width_only,width_to_depth`, surface `active`; recovery wrapper changes to repo root, uses the same task/surface defaults and defaults results to `Results/massive_opf_suite_recovery`, then execs the massive wrapper. All use `set -euo pipefail` and forward arguments untouched.
- `scripts/kill_all_runners.py` is a separate force-kill emergency utility, not the normal watchdog. It owns only commands whose basename is a recognized launcher/runner entrypoint and that also carry the expected marker (`--mode`, `--model`, or `--`). It additionally requires cwd under the copied repository root or that root in the command line. For each owned process other than itself, it enumerates descendants recursively, reverses the child list, force-kills each unique PID and then the root, swallowing process-gone/access/zombie errors; it has no graceful TERM, wait, PID file, or run-ID restriction. It counts successful `kill()` calls and prints the total.
- The README's descriptive case/model counts and smoke-validation claims are not runtime evidence for this audit. Model-specific material is excluded from this ledger.

| `utils/opf_suite_launcher.py`, `utils/opf_massive_suite_runner.py`, defaults, pressure wrapper, bundle, runtime tuning, backend guard, logging context, process cleanup | Sections 1-19; central scheduler line/function coverage is itemized in Sections 16-18. |

This boundary table is a scope map, not a claim that task-data files were exhaustively documented. The requested orchestration paths, shared state-transfer utilities, and outer supervisors are the code coverage target; task-data construction and model implementation behavior are not.

## 24. Backend admission and logging side effects

These helpers are not schedulers, but they enforce the child environment the scheduler selects and annotate its logs.

- `ml_backends._backend_context()` is the tuple `(cpu_admitted, gpu_admitted, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES)`. CPU admission is true for backend `cpu`, any of the three truthy CPU flags, or a present CUDA visibility value that trims to empty/`-1`. GPU admission is true only for backend exactly `gpu`. Contradictory admission raises. Once GPU probing or any accelerator status succeeded, changing admission/visibility requires a fresh process; an all-false cached status may be cleared and recomputed.
- `gpu_available()` refuses a CPU-admitted worker, then probes Torch by allocating/filling one CUDA element and synchronizing. Import/runtime/OS/attribute failures fall through to CuPy, which must report at least one device and pass a one-byte allocation/fill/device-sync. Successful probe stores the exact admission context. `enable_optional_gpu_accelerators()` memoizes status for that context, errors when a GPU-admitted child has no usable Torch/CuPy runtime, and otherwise returns four booleans: GPU usable, cuDF pandas hook, cuML hook, CuPy usable.
- Optional cuDF pandas installation is refused with warning if `pandas` is already imported. cuML installation is refused if `sklearn`, `umap`, or `hdbscan` is already imported. Missing packages silently disable that hook; other activation errors warn and return false. `backend_pandas()` triggers this hook before importing pandas.
- `array_module` checks all passed objects against CPU admission, imports/probes CuPy, and returns CuPy only if a supplied value is a CuPy object; otherwise NumPy. `as_numpy` uses `cupy.asnumpy` for CuPy values when usable and otherwise `numpy.asarray`. `as_cupy` returns `cupy.asarray` only when cached status says CuPy available; otherwise it returns a NumPy array. CPU admission rejects CuPy objects and tensors whose `.device.type` is cuda/mps/xpu/hip before inspection or conversion.
- Seed resolution precedence is explicit convertible integer, convertible nonempty `OPF_ADP_GLOBAL_SEED`, then 42. `seed_everything` writes `PYTHONHASHSEED`, seeds Python and NumPy, seeds CuPy if available, and seeds only Torch CPU's default generator when CPU-admitted; otherwise it calls `torch.manual_seed` and `torch.cuda.manual_seed_all` when CUDA is available.
- The optional accuracy helper supports Torch, CuPy, and NumPy values; for multi-column predictions and labels it applies argmax on the last axis, flattens, compares equality, and returns the mean as float. `iter_backend_names` yields four status strings. These helpers are child-library support, not runner job-selection logic.
- Logging's default context samples host total/used/available through psutil and, when Torch CUDA is usable, calls `torch.cuda.mem_get_info(current_device)` and reports one GPU-running process. Exceptions are swallowed and values remain zero. Installing the record factory wraps the prior factory; for every log record it computes default context, calls the configurable provider, overlays a returned dict, and attaches each key/value. Provider failures are ignored. Therefore even a custom central scheduler provider does not prevent the default host/GPU sampling attempt first.
- Console/root logging handlers write to stdout, use timestamp format `%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S`, include level/name/message plus GPU/CPU counts and used/total GPU/RAM MiB. A handler is added only if no existing `StreamHandler` is present. Named console loggers disable propagation; root logging does not.

## 25. Dispatcher audit delta: import, argument, and nested-child edge cases

The final pass over all of `universal_main.py` found several handoff details that were not explicit in the earlier summary. These concern process/argument orchestration only; algorithm aliases and training behavior remain outside scope.

- Import-time order is significant: `torch` and the shared epoch parser are imported before runtime bootstrap; `bootstrap_runtime("universal_main")` runs before optional accelerator initialization; then `DNN/VANILLA` is appended to `sys.path`, and Torch's default dtype is set to float64 before registry construction. The bootstrap warning catches only `ImportError`; other bootstrap exceptions can abort import. Optional accelerator setup also catches only `ImportError` at this call site, although the helper itself handles its own expected probe cases.
- `ModelRegistry.root` is the caller's current working directory, not the source file directory. Canonical discovery imports the vanilla `MODEL_MODULES` registry and uses `importlib.util.find_spec`; fallback paths are then based on that root. Import failures of the canonical registry are swallowed and leave an empty canonical map, after which fallback scanning still runs. Registry insertion is first-name-wins; aliases do not replace an existing registration. A missing/unknown requested name prints an error and exits 1; `--list` prints the sorted registry and returns without dispatch; no model prints help and exits 1.
- The dispatcher uses `parse_known_args`, so unrecognized tokens survive for child handling. `parse_unknown_kv_args` splits only at the first `=`, parses digit-only values as integers and a single-dot digit form as float, otherwise keeps text; non-assignment tokens are omitted from that helper's dictionary. Native execution independently repeats that conversion while building config, warns and discards non-assignment tokens, adds its package and script-parent directories to `sys.path`, registers the loaded module in `sys.modules` before execution, and requires `run_pipeline`. Results and seed environment variables are assigned before module execution. Optional native values (`max_epochs`, batch size and lambda values) are inserted only when truthy, which means explicit zero is dropped; unknown key/value settings are applied afterward and can override prior config values. ADP defaults use `setdefault`, so user-supplied values win.
- Ported execution first adds standard flags only for truthy parsed options (except seed, which is always included), then appends every unknown token unchanged. It separately parses unknown assignments solely to suppress generated ADP defaults; an unknown `max_epochs=0` suppresses the generated max-epoch flag. It starts the nested command with the current interpreter and `-u`, merges stderr into stdout, enables text line buffering, and creates `logs/` relative to current working directory. Log names have one-second timestamp precision and open in write mode, so two same-model launches in that second can target the same file. Each line is echoed and flushed to dispatcher stdout and written/flushed to the nested log. The outer scheduler's per-job log receives the echoed stream.
- The nested ported process gets a copied environment with results and seed variables assigned; native execution instead mutates the dispatcher's own environment and runs in-process. Ported execution starts a new POSIX session, allowing the dispatcher's signal handler to signal the process group; on Windows only the direct process handle is terminated/killed. The handler sends TERM, polls the direct process every 0.1 seconds up to at least 0.1 seconds (default 10), then sends KILL and clears the global handle without a final wait. If the child exits during the poll, the handle is cleared and the handler returns. A ported nonzero exit is propagated with `sys.exit(returncode)`; signal handling exits 130. The main execution block catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and routes it through the same handler.
- This also clarifies a boundary in the parent scheduler: its launch handle supervises the dispatcher PID/process group; the dispatcher's nested ported process is separately supervised by the dispatcher's signal path. A crash that bypasses that path can leave nested-process cleanup dependent on OS/session behavior rather than an explicit dispatcher `finally` block.
